properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research, specifically Zep/Graphiti, described there as "temporal knowledge graphs that encode what happened, when, and how entities relate over time" for agents that "must reason about evolving facts". Graphiti's distinguishing feature in that family is BI-TEMPORALITY: every fact carries both when it was true in the world and when the system came to know it. STILL OPEN.

WHAT REFLOW2 HAS, CHECKED IN schema/temporal.yaml RATHER THAN RECALLED: TemporalFact carries VALID_FROM and VALID_TO, both pointing at a DesignEpoch, plus `basis: measured|forecast` and an author-stated `confidence`. So the design already models world-time properly, and BL-68 already separated observation from projection — which is the harder half of what Graphiti does and reflow2 got there independently. What TemporalFact does NOT carry is any epoch for when the assertion ENTERED the record. ChangeEvent has `detected_at`, DriftEvent has `detected_at`, DimensionObservation has `observed_at` — the arrival time exists on the EVENTS but not on the FACT.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this may be worth more than schema tidiness: a retroactively discovered fact is written with VALID_FROM at the epoch it became true, and the record then reads as though the design always knew. "The beamline analysis code has assumed a single detector since 2016" and "we discovered in August 2026 that the beamline analysis code has assumed a single detector since 2016" become the same node. The second is the more useful sentence, because it tells a reader that everything designed between 2016 and 2026 was designed in ignorance of it — and that is exactly the reasoning a brownfield adoption needs. This is Anthony's own operating context (a ten-year-old bluesky/tiled stack being evolved on the fly), not a hypothetical.

WHERE IT ALREADY BITES, POSSIBLY: cap:as-of-epoch answers "what did the design say at epoch n" from snapshots. If retroactive facts are written with early VALID_FROM, an as-of-epoch answer can attribute knowledge to a past epoch that nobody had then — a subtler version of the same fiction dec:readiness-forecast-is-a-temporal-fact was created to stop. NOT VERIFIED: whether as-of-epoch actually reads TemporalFact validity or only Snapshots was not checked, and that determines whether this is a live defect or only a modelling gap. Check before treating it as either.

WHAT IS CHEAP: adding a RECORDED_AT epoch edge (or reusing AT_EPOCH, which already means "belongs to" for Snapshot and ChangeEvent) is additive, and req:defaults-do-not-assert has a clean answer for the backfill — absent means unstated, which reads as unstated.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: nothing currently READS TemporalFact validity for anything a user sees, and reflow2's record already has a long list of declared-and-read-by-nothing fields (embedding_field, Project.domain) that this would join. A second time axis is also a real conceptual cost on a vocabulary that is already large, and the honest test is whether any computation would use it — which is the same bar dec:exploratory-staging is being held to. If the answer is "only a human reading the node would notice", the cheaper fix is prose in the fact's statement, not schema.
properties.name: OPEN — should a TemporalFact record WHEN IT WAS LEARNED as well as when it was true, since VALID_FROM/VALID_TO carry only world-time and a retroactive discovery loses its own arrival?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea because the missing half was verified in the schema and the brownfield consequence is Anthony's actual working context, but the deciding test — does any computation read it — is unanswered, and that test is what dec:exploratory-staging established as the bar for new vocabulary. Also recorded because BL-68 already made the harder measured/forecast distinction, which makes this the same argument one step along rather than a new idea.
